One: "And indeed he, because of his love of wealth, is stingy." This is the view of al-Hasan, Ibn Qutaybah, (p-211) and al-Zajjaj. Abu 'Ubaydah said: "shadid" and "mutashaddid" are also said of the stingy. Tarafah said:

"I see death seizing the noble and choosing the precious wealth of the stingy, tight-fisted one."

The second: "And indeed he is intensely loving of good." This is the choice of al-Farra'. He said: since the word "love" came first in the phrase, and the original place of "intense" was to be joined to it, the word "love" was omitted from the end because its mention came at the beginning, and for the sake of the verse-endings. A similar example is ﴿The wind has blown violently on a stormy day﴾ [Ibrahim: 18]; since "wind" was mentioned before "day," it was dropped from the end.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered﴾ — meaning: the mentioned man; ﴿and what is within the breasts is obtained﴾ — i.e., it is made manifest and brought out. "Tahsil" is the distinguishing of what is obtained. Ibn 'Abbas said: what is in them is brought forth. Ibn Qutaybah said: what is in them of good and evil is distinguished. Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi said: the meaning is: if the disbelieving man knew what he would have on that day, he would renounce disbelief and hasten to Islam. Then He began, saying: ﴿Indeed, their Lord, that Day, is fully Aware of them.﴾ Others said: "inna" was read with a kasra only because of the lam; otherwise it would be fathah, due to the verb of knowing taking it as object.

(p-212) If it is said: Is Allah not Aware of them in every state? Why did He specify that day?

The answer: the meaning is that He will recompense them for their deeds on that day. A similar usage is ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾ [An-Nisa: 63], meaning He will recompense them for it. Similarly: ﴿The Day they will come forth, nothing of them will be concealed from Allah﴾ [Ghafir: 16].
